ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Objects A and B placed on a sufficiently long wooden board are made of the same material, and the surface roughness is the same. They are now moving with the long wooden board at speed v to the right in uniform rectilinear motion, as shown in the figure. At a certain moment the wooden board suddenly stops moving. It is known that $m_A>m_B$. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Regardless of whether the wooden board is smooth, the relative distance between A and B remains unchanged.

They are now moving with the long wooden board at speed v to the right in uniform rectilinear motion, as shown in the figure. At a certain moment the wooden board suddenly stops moving. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontally placed long wooden board, with two small objects placed on the board, the left one labeled A and the right one labeled B; at the right end of the wooden board there is a velocity arrow pointing to the right, labeled v, indicating that the wooden board and A and B on it originally moved together to the right in uniform motion. Reasoning: Before the wooden board suddenly stops, both A and B move with the wooden board, so their initial velocities are the same, both v to the right. The problem states that A and B are made of the same material, and the surface roughness is the same, so if there is friction between them and the wooden board, their coefficients of kinetic friction are the same. Discussion by cases: 1. If the wooden board is smooth, after the wooden board stops, A and B are not acted on by friction in the horizontal direction, and still both move uniformly to the right with speed v. Their velocities are always the same, so the relative distance does not change. 2. If the wooden board is rough, after the wooden board stops, A and B slide to the right relative to the wooden board and are subjected to sliding friction to the left. For A, f_A=μm_Ag, so a_A=f_A/m_A=μg; for B, f_B=μm_Bg, so a_B=f_B/m_B=μg. Although m_A>m_B, the mass is canceled when finding the acceleration, so their decelerations are the same. Also because their initial velocities are both v, their deceleration processes are completely the same, and the stopping time and sliding displacement are also the same, so the relative distance still does not change. Therefore, regardless of whether the wooden board is smooth, after the wooden board stops, the relative distance between A and B remains unchanged.
